setup_tiers.description: Runtime attach only: an agent flag, a preload require, the CLR profiler environment, a php.ini extension. No application source involved.
A boot-file initializer loads and configures the tool before application code runs (Ruby's require+configure pattern, Elastic Python's middleware). Request-path code is untouched.
Source is untouched but the build command is wrapped by a compile-time weaver (`orchestrion go build`, `go tool otelc go build`) that injects instrumentation during compilation.
Instrumentation is woven into application code: wrappers at every client/server construction site and contexts threaded through (Go contribs, Rust propagator API with hand-written carriers).

annotations.title: Baseline: with no agent attached, nothing propagates
annotations.cause: These relays run with no agent, wrapper or tracing library; no runtime in the matrix carries context on its own except .NET over HTTP/gRPC.
annotations.explanation:
Control runs: every language's relay with no agent, wrapper or tracing gem
attached (`none-*` variants, 128 hops). Java, Node, Python, Go, Ruby, Rust
and PHP behave as expected — nothing propagates on any of the 16 boundaries
for any header — confirming that the instrumented results are attributable
to the tool under test, not to the apps or the harness.

.NET is the partial exception: with no agent, ASP.NET Core hosting creates an
`Activity` per request and `HttpClient`'s DiagnosticsHandler injects it on the
way out (gRPC inherits this because `Grpc.Net.Client` rides on HttpClient),
so `traceparent` (same trace-id, fresh span-id) and `tracestate` (preserved
verbatim) pass on all four `http/grpc -> http/grpc` boundaries. There is no
built-in messaging propagation, so every Kafka and RabbitMQ leg is dark on
.NET too, and `ot-baggage-*` is never handled. The built-in `baggage`
behaviour on the HTTP/gRPC legs is described separately
(`baseline-dotnet-baggage-reemitted-as-correlation-context`).

annotations.title: Baseline .NET 8: the runtime reads W3C baggage but re-emits it as Correlation-Context
annotations.cause: On .NET 8/9 the default DistributedContextPropagator is the pre-W3C legacy one: it reads `baggage` but re-emits it as the obsolete Correlation-Context header.
annotations.explanation:
With no agent attached, .NET 8 propagates `traceparent` and `tracestate`
across `http/grpc -> http/grpc`, and it *does* read the incoming W3C
`baggage` header into `Activity.Baggage` — but the default
`DistributedContextPropagator` on .NET 8/9 is the pre-W3C "legacy"
propagator, which re-emits baggage under the obsolete draft name
`Correlation-Context`. Values survive one hop and are then invisible to any
W3C-only reader downstream, so the harness scores `baggage` absent.

Version dependence: .NET 10 switches the default to a strict W3C propagator
(`baggage` header out, strict encoding, `CreatePreW3CPropagator()` to opt
back) — an uninstrumented .NET service changes its propagation behaviour on
a runtime upgrade. Harness runs used .NET 8.

links.title: .NET 10 breaking change: default trace context propagator

annotations.title: PHP: no gRPC server exists in any tracer-supported topology, so gRPC-inbound is undeliverable
annotations.cause: The official gRPC PHP implementation is client-only; the harness's Apache mod_php + CLI worker topology cannot accept gRPC calls, so grpc->* hops never run.
annotations.explanation:
grpc.io's PHP quickstart: "You can only create gRPC clients in PHP. Use
another language to create a gRPC server." (Restated in grpc/grpc #38481,
open, filed by a Google engineer.) PHP *can* serve gRPC through a separate
application server — RoadRunner's gRPC plugin (Go proxy → PHP workers) or
Swoole-based frameworks such as Hyperf — but none of the tracers'
zero-code instrumentation covers those paths: dd-trace-php's RoadRunner
integration hooks the HTTP `PSR7Worker` only (Datadog's guidance for
RoadRunner gRPC is manual `dd_trace_method` hooks, dd-trace-php #805); OTel
has no roadrunner-grpc PHP instrumentation (RoadRunner's `otel` plugin
traces in the Go proxy layer, not the PHP worker); Elastic and New Relic
support neither.

The harness measures the documented Apache mod_php + two CLI workers
topology, the supported deployment for all three tracers (dd-trace-php does
not support `php -S`), so every `grpc->*` boundary is undelivered for every
PHP variant including the baseline. A RoadRunner-based relay with manual
instrumentation is a candidate follow-up (see the roadmap in DESIGN.md).

annotations.title: PHP: no tool instruments the ext-grpc client, so every *->grpc leg is header-free
annotations.cause: Neither OTel PHP, dd-trace-php, Elastic PHP nor New Relic PHP hooks ext-grpc + grpc/grpc client calls; no metadata is injected on any *->grpc boundary.
annotations.explanation:
Every `*->grpc` cell is header-free for otel, datadog, elastic and newrelic
alike: the outbound gRPC client (`ext-grpc` + `grpc/grpc`) is not on any
tool's instrumentation list, so nothing is injected into call metadata.

Datadog: dd-trace-php #916 is the canonical gRPC request, open since 2020
and marked "up-for-grabs" ("We do not have enough bandwidth to work on this
integration during this quarter"); gRPC is absent from Datadog's PHP
compatibility tables. OpenTelemetry: the opentelemetry-php-contrib
instrumentation tree (30 auto-instrumentations) contains no gRPC entry —
gRPC exists in the OTel PHP ecosystem only as the OTLP *export* transport;
no issue proposes instrumenting `ext-grpc` client calls (filing candidate).
Elastic and New Relic list ext-grpc as unsupported.

Workaround: add the propagation headers to the call's metadata array
yourself at every gRPC call site, using the tool's propagator/inject API.

annotations.title: Go build-time weavers: Kafka consumers never hand the extracted context back to application code
annotations.cause: otelc's kafka-go Reader has no callback to hand back the context; Orchestrion's sarama consumer weave does not continue the trace seeded in record headers.
annotations.explanation:
Both compile-time weavers break at the same place runtime agents do: the
consume side of an async hop. Both compile deliberately naive apps (single
`main.go`, zero tracing imports); only the build command differs from an
uninstrumented build.

**otel-go-compiletime** (otelc v1.1.0): kafka-go's `Reader` is a pull-style
API (`ReadMessage(ctx)` in an app-owned loop) with no callback boundary, so
the woven consumer instrumentation has nowhere to hand the extracted context
back to application code. The app's loop context is `context.Background()`
and outbound calls carry nothing — not even a new trace (with no valid span
context the W3C propagator injects nothing). PR #1076 confirms a consume
span is created per `FetchMessage`; the missing half is activation, not
extraction. Issue #695 (open) is the maintainer-acknowledged messaging
semconv workstream naming this gap ("a process-span story for the zero-code
gap") and planning IBM/sarama next. By contrast, the same variant carries
baggage *into* Kafka with zero source changes, because kafka-go's
`Writer.WriteMessages(ctx, …)` takes a context.

**datadog-go-orchestrion** (v1.13.0, dd-trace-go v2.10.1, IBM/sarama
v1.60.2): the woven consumer-group instrumentation does not continue the
trace seeded in the record headers, so outbound calls after a consume carry
`x-datadog-*`/`traceparent` with a fresh trace-id; baggage, `ot-baggage-*`
and the foreign tracestate entry are gone. The hand-wired `datadog-go` relay
passes the same legs with the same library versions by following the
dd-trace-go contrib README (extract-and-activate in the handler). No issue
reports the Orchestrion sarama consume gap — filing candidate.

What a user can do: extract from the record headers and set the context in
the consume loop/handler yourself — the one step neither weaver can see.

annotations.title: Go build-time weavers: neither otelc nor dd-trace-go has an AMQP client integration to weave
annotations.cause: otelc's supported-libraries list has no AMQP client and dd-trace-go has no amqp091 contrib, so RabbitMQ publish injects nothing and consume extracts nothing.
annotations.explanation:
Coverage is an allowlist, and neither weaver's allowlist includes the
amqp091 client. otelc's getting-started supported-libraries table lists
`segmentio/kafka-go` as its only messaging client — no sarama, no franz-go,
no AMQP. dd-trace-go has no amqp091/RabbitMQ contrib, so Orchestrion has
nothing to enable on RabbitMQ legs.

Nothing is injected on `*->rabbitmq`. On `rabbitmq->*` the consumer runs
with no incoming context; where the outbound client *is* woven (HTTP, gRPC,
Kafka on Orchestrion) it emits a fresh root trace, and otherwise nothing.
The hand-wired `otel-go` and `datadog-go` relays pass all RabbitMQ legs with
hand-written AMQP carriers — the same manual step a weaver cannot supply for
a library it does not know.

annotations.title: OpenTelemetry, Elastic APM and New Relic never implemented the OpenTracing-era ot-baggage-* headers
annotations.cause: ot-baggage-* is a legacy OpenTracing convention; OpenTelemetry, Elastic APM and New Relic each define their propagation header set without it.
annotations.explanation:
The seeded `ot-baggage-sd-routing-key` header is ignored — neither extracted
nor re-emitted — by every OpenTelemetry, Elastic and New Relic variant on
every delivered boundary. None of these tools ever emitted the OpenTracing
header format: OpenTelemetry standardised on W3C `baggage`; Elastic's agent
spec defines `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage` and the binary
`elasticapmtraceparent`; New Relic's distributed-tracing model is
`traceparent`, `tracestate` and the vendor `newrelic` header.

The header outlives its deprecation only in Datadog's Java, Node and Go
tracers, where it crosses all 16 boundaries as legacy behaviour of the
`datadog` style (see `datadog-ot-baggage-not-implemented` for the Datadog
tracers that do not carry it). Where a tool propagates W3C `baggage`, the
same values travel there instead.

links.title: How New Relic distributed tracing works

annotations.title: dd-trace-java injects W3C baggage only on HTTP clients
annotations.cause: Non-HTTP client and messaging producer instrumentations inject from the span, not the current context, so the context-scoped baggage propagator finds nothing.
annotations.explanation:
With `DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE=datadog,tracecontext,baggage` (and with
agent defaults), dd-trace-java 1.65.1 propagates W3C `baggage` on
`http->http` only. `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `ot-baggage-*` and
`x-datadog-*` cross all 16 boundaries — the trace survives, the baggage does
not, which makes the failure invisible to trace-waterfall debugging.

Root cause: Kafka/AMQP producer and non-HTTP client instrumentations call
`defaultPropagator().inject(span, ...)`. Baggage lives on the thread-local
context, and `AgentSpan.get()` delegates non-span context keys to
`Context.root()` rather than `Context.current()`, so the baggage propagator
sees an empty context. Datadog confirmed the scoping on #11286 ("W3C baggage
propagation was specifically scoped to HTTP to begin with"; "Kafka
instrumentation is indeed dropping all context elements except tracing at
injection"). A community fix (PR #11330) documented the root cause exactly
but was closed unmerged. Datadog's context-centric migration (PR #12027,
PR #12033, merged Jul 2026; groundwork in PR #8330 / PR #10767) so far
covers async/HTTP paths only.

What a user can do: the legacy `ot-baggage-*` headers cross all 16
boundaries in this agent, or inject `baggage` manually at messaging and gRPC
call sites. Upstream fix: inject from `Context.current()` at the messaging
and gRPC inject sites. Only the Kafka case is reported (#11286); the gRPC
and RabbitMQ measurements appear unreported — filing candidate.

links.title: dd-trace-java #11510 (same class on Spring WebClient, fixed)

annotations.title: dd-trace-py: Kafka header injection is disabled by default
annotations.cause: ddtrace's Kafka integration ships distributed_tracing_enabled=False; nothing is injected into produced records until DD_KAFKA_PROPAGATION_ENABLED=true.
annotations.explanation:
With default configuration ddtrace 4.14.0 injects *no propagation headers of
any kind* into produced Kafka records, so every `*->kafka` cell is absent.
This is a documented default-off: `ddtrace.config.kafka["distributed_tracing_enabled"]`
is "Default: False" (env `DD_KAFKA_PROPAGATION_ENABLED`), introduced that
way in PR #7434 "to prevent any unexpected changes to users' kafka tracing".

Setting `DD_KAFKA_PROPAGATION_ENABLED=true` turns on full W3C injection
including baggage — the `datadog-python-kafkaprop` variant measures this and
passes `http->kafka` and `grpc->kafka`. The consume side remains broken with
the flag on (see `datadog-python-kafka-consume-no-activation`).

annotations.title: dd-trace-py: consumed Kafka context is not activated for the code that processes the message
annotations.cause: ddtrace's kafka.consume span is created without using the extracted context, so downstream calls start a new trace and baggage is dropped.
annotations.explanation:
Even with `DD_KAFKA_PROPAGATION_ENABLED=true`, `kafka->*` starts a new trace
(traceparent carries a fresh trace-id, the foreign tracestate entry is lost,
baggage is gone). A Datadog engineer's own description in PR #7345:
"`kafka.consume` and `kafka.produce` spans are not connected … because the
context isn't used when the `kafka.consume` span is created."

User-report trail: #8967 (flag on, traces still detached; the workaround is
`tracer.context_provider.activate(Propagator.extract(dict(msg.headers())))`)
and #17980 (open, on batch-activation semantics). Datadog is now migrating
consume to links-instead-of-continuation behind a config
(`propagation_as_span_links`; PR #18667, PR #19858: "We can't do that directly
because we would break existing semantics").

Workaround: extract and activate manually after `poll()`, as in #8967. No
upstream issue covers the *baggage* dimension of this gap (existing issues
cover trace identity only).

annotations.title: dd-trace-py has no pika integration; RabbitMQ legs lose everything
annotations.cause: ddtrace's only AMQP coverage is the kombu library; pika is not instrumented, so nothing is injected on publish or extracted on consume.
annotations.explanation:
Nothing is injected on any `*->rabbitmq` leg and nothing is extracted on any
`rabbitmq->*` leg, flag or no flag. dd-trace-py's AMQP coverage is `kombu`
only (and kombu is not auto-patched); pika has zero mentions in the Python
compatibility docs. Datadog's disposition in #2047 (2021): "The request for
a pika integration is in our team's feature backlog and is not planned for
the short term." aio-pika was re-requested in #17225 (open, Mar 2026),
which confirms kombu-only AMQP coverage.

Where the outbound client is instrumented (`rabbitmq->http`, `rabbitmq->grpc`)
a fresh trace is injected; where it is not (`rabbitmq->kafka`,
`rabbitmq->rabbitmq`) nothing is. Workaround: inject into message properties
on publish and use the same manual
`tracer.context_provider.activate(Propagator.extract(...))` pattern as the
Kafka workaround in the consumer callback. Uninstrumented library ⇒ silent
total loss.

annotations.title: dd-trace-py: ot-baggage-* inject and extract are gated behind a default-off flag
annotations.cause: ddtrace has ot-baggage-* code, but both inject and extract require DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_HTTP_BAGGAGE_ENABLED=true (default False).
annotations.explanation:
dd-trace-py's `propagation/http.py` handles `ot-baggage-*` only when
`config._propagation_http_baggage_enabled` is true. The flag
`DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_HTTP_BAGGAGE_ENABLED` defaults to False; it was added
in v2.4.0 (PR #6072) explicitly "to have baggage item support … compatible
with other language DataDog tracing libs e.g. java, nodejs". The other
historical `ot-baggage` path, the OpenTracing bridge, was removed in v3.0.0.

The seeded `ot-baggage-*` header is therefore ignored — neither extracted nor
re-emitted — on all 16 boundaries. The values still flow via W3C `baggage`
where that works. Enabling the flag is expected to restore the header on
HTTP; the harness has not measured the flag, and whether it applies to
non-HTTP carriers is not covered by our references. Datadog's propagation
reference documents no `ot-baggage` style at all.

annotations.title: dd-trace .NET, Ruby, Rust and PHP do not emit the legacy ot-baggage-* headers
annotations.cause: ot-baggage-* is undocumented legacy behaviour of dd-trace java/js/go; .NET never had it, Ruby removed it with OpenTracing, Rust and PHP do not emit it.
annotations.explanation:
dd-trace-java, dd-trace-js and dd-trace-go carry `ot-baggage-*` across all
16 boundaries; these four tracers ignore the seeded header (not extracted,
not re-emitted). Datadog's propagation reference lists the styles `datadog`,
`tracecontext`, `b3single`, `b3multi`, `baggage`, `none` — `ot-baggage`
appears nowhere, so the headers the first group emits are legacy behaviour
of their `datadog` style rather than a configurable format.

Per tracer: dd-trace-rb removed OpenTracing (and with it `ot-baggage-*`) in
2.0 (PR #3443; maintainer confirmation in #4055 — W3C baggage landed later in
2.13.0 via #4493/#4505). dd-trace-dotnet never had it — a code search for
`ot-baggage` returns zero results. datadog-opentelemetry (Rust) has no
`ot-baggage-*` style. dd-trace-php *can* emit `ot-baggage-*` in some
configurations (#3614, nginx rejecting `ot-baggage-true-client-ip`), so
"never emits" would overstate — but at 1.25.0 with the harness configuration
it measured absent on every delivered boundary.

The values still flow via W3C `baggage` wherever that header works for the
same tracer.

annotations.title: dd-trace-rb has no bunny integration; RabbitMQ legs lose everything
annotations.cause: The datadog gem's AMQP coverage is the Sneakers/Kicks worker framework only; the bunny client is not instrumented on publish or consume.
annotations.explanation:
All HTTP, gRPC and Kafka boundaries pass (W3C baggage included) on datadog
2.42.0. RabbitMQ: nothing is injected on publish, and consume does not
extract, so `rabbitmq->http/grpc/kafka` start a fresh trace on the outbound
leg and `rabbitmq->rabbitmq` carries nothing. The dd-trace-rb compatibility
list has no bunny entry (AMQP coverage exists only via Sneakers/Kicks), and
the contrib source tree confirms no bunny integration exists in code.

Workaround: inject the trace context into message headers on publish and
continue the trace from them in the consumer block yourself. No feature
request for bunny exists upstream at all — filing candidate. Same class as
dd-trace-py/pika: canonical client, zero coverage.

annotations.title: dd-trace-php closes the rdkafka consume span inside consume(), before user code runs
annotations.cause: The Kafka consume hook attaches the extracted headers to a span it closes before returning the message, so outbound calls run outside the extracted context.
annotations.explanation:
Kafka *injection* works on dd-trace-php 1.25.0 (`*->kafka` passes, baggage
included), but the rdkafka *consume* side does not continue context:
`kafka->*` starts a new trace and baggage is gone. The mechanism is visible
in `KafkaIntegration.php`: the consume hook opens a new trace root, attaches
the extracted headers to *that span*, and calls `close_span()` inside the
`consume()` call itself — before application code ever sees the message.

`DD_TRACE_KAFKA_DISTRIBUTED_TRACING` defaults to true (`configuration.h`), so
the gap is the scoping, not the flag. The historical rdkafka request (#639)
was never closed after injection shipped.

Workaround: read the record headers after `consume()` returns and continue
the trace from them manually before outbound calls. Upstream fix: keep the
consume span (and the extracted context) active until the application has
processed the message. No upstream issue reports that consumed Kafka context
does not reach post-consume user code — filing candidate.

annotations.title: Orchestrion: sarama SendMessage has no context parameter, so the woven produce span is a new root
annotations.cause: Orchestrion finds a context.Context only in the woven function's parameters; sarama's SendMessage(msg) has none, so the produce span is a new root.
annotations.explanation:
`datadog-go-orchestrion` (Orchestrion v1.13.0 weaving dd-trace-go v2.10.1,
same IBM/sarama v1.60.2 as the hand-wired `datadog-go` relay) passes all four
`http/grpc -> http/grpc` legs with baggage and `ot-baggage-*`. Into Kafka,
headers are *present* but carry a brand-new trace-id: `x-datadog-*` and
`traceparent` arrive with a fresh trace, the foreign tracestate entry is
replaced, and baggage is gone.

Orchestrion's advice templates resolve a `context.Context` only from the
innermost function's parameter list (orchestrion #871). sarama's
`SyncProducer.SendMessage(msg)` takes no context at all, so the woven
producer starts a *root* produce span and injects that. The hand-wired relay
passes these legs with identical library versions because the dd-trace-go
contrib pattern injects from the request context before `SendMessage`.

Workaround: follow the contrib IBM/sarama README and inject from `ctx` into
the message before `SendMessage` (one manual step). Upstream: a
context-carrying producer API, or weaver support for goroutine-local context
at sites with no ctx parameter. A related operational note: `orchestrion
pin` prints a spurious "removing unnecessary import" warning against the
published `all/v2` module; cosmetic, build unaffected — filing candidate.

annotations.title: apm-agent-go has no baggage API, by explicit decision
annotations.cause: Elastic's Go agent carries trace identity on all 16 boundaries but implements no W3C baggage at all; the request was closed not-planned in 2019.
annotations.explanation:
`apmhttp`/`apmgrpc` wrappers plus the documented manual traceparent/tracestate
pattern carry trace identity across all 16 boundaries on apm-agent-go
v2.7.12, but the agent has no baggage API. This was declined upstream:
apm-agent-go #537 was closed not-planned ("no plans for baggage at the
moment"), and `apmot/span.go` states "SetBaggageItem is a no-op; we do not
support baggage" (`apmot/doc.go`: "Things not implemented by this tracer:
binary propagation format, baggage, logging"). A repo-wide search hits
baggage only in the OpenTracing bridge — there is no W3C baggage code.

This contradicts Elastic's own agent spec ("Agents MUST parse, validate, and
attach the `baggage` header according to the W3C specification"). A user who
needs baggage must carry it as an application header on every hop
themselves.

annotations.title: Elastic Node, Python, Ruby and PHP agents do not propagate W3C baggage on any boundary
annotations.cause: Only Elastic's Java agent (and .NET over HTTP/gRPC) implements the baggage propagation the agent spec mandates; these agents drop it on every boundary.
annotations.explanation:
Elastic's agent spec mandates baggage support, but only the Java agent
delivers it end-to-end. elastic-apm-node 4.18.0 has no W3C baggage
implementation; elastic-apm (Python) 6.26.2, elastic-apm (Ruby) 4.9.0 and
elastic_apm (PHP) 1.17.0 measure `baggage` absent on every boundary,
including `http->http` where `traceparent`/`tracestate` continue. The
seeded member is neither extracted nor re-emitted.

Outside Java, Elastic APM cannot currently carry application baggage across
protocol boundaries; a user must forward the `baggage` header as an
application header themselves. Elastic's Node distributed-tracing docs
likewise describe manual `traceparent` passing only (no tracestate or
baggage). Our references record no upstream issue requesting W3C baggage in
these agents.

links.title: Elastic Node.js agent — distributed tracing docs

annotations.title: elastic-apm-node does not instrument amqplib; RabbitMQ legs carry nothing
annotations.cause: amqplib is absent from the Node agent's supported technologies; long-standing requests (#1188, #1791) have been open since 2019/2020.
annotations.explanation:
elastic-apm-node 4.18.0 propagates `traceparent` and `tracestate` over
HTTP, gRPC and kafkajs, but amqplib is absent from the supported-technologies
page, so nothing is injected on `*->rabbitmq` and nothing is extracted on
`rabbitmq->*`. Elastic's docs direct queue users to manual `traceparent`
passing (the recipe carries `traceparent` only).

The amqplib requests #1188 (Jul 2019) and #1791 (Jul 2020) remain open.
Workaround: pass `traceparent`/`tracestate` in message headers yourself and
start the consumer transaction with the received `traceparent`.

annotations.title: elastic-apm Python: gRPC server interceptor assigns the tracestate header name instead of its value
annotations.cause: server_interceptor.py has `tracestate = metadata.key`, so after a gRPC hop the outbound tracestate is the literal string 'tracestate'; foreign entries are lost.
annotations.explanation:
gRPC-inbound continues the trace (`traceparent` passes) but drops foreign
`tracestate` entries: the outbound `tracestate` header emitted after a gRPC
hop is the literal string `tracestate`. The root cause is a one-line bug in
`elasticapm/contrib/grpc/server_interceptor.py` (v6.26.2, lines 66–73):
`elif metadata.key == "tracestate": tracestate = metadata.key` — the header
*name* is assigned instead of its value. Still unfixed on main (file last
touched Oct 2023).

Bonus finding for the same report: the async variant
(`async_server_interceptor.py`) never reads `invocation_metadata` at all, so
the async gRPC server path does not extract trace context, period.

Unreported upstream — filing candidate with the one-line fix
(`metadata.key` → `metadata.value`). This is the only tracestate corruption
observed among all tracers that continued a trace.

annotations.title: elastic-apm Python has no confluent-kafka or pika instrumentation
annotations.cause: The Python agent's only messaging client is kafka-python; confluent-kafka and pika are uninstrumented: nothing is injected, consumers start no transaction.
annotations.explanation:
The Python supported-technologies page lists `kafka-python` (>=2.0,<3) as
its only messaging client; confluent-kafka and pika appear nowhere. On
elastic-apm 6.26.2 nothing is injected into produced Kafka records or
published AMQP messages, and consumers start no transaction — so even the
outbound HTTP/gRPC calls after a consume carry no headers at all (absent,
not a new trace).

RabbitMQ has been requested since Dec 2019 (#678: "It would be of high value
to add instrumentation and distributed tracing for message brokers and, in
particular, RabbitMQ"), still open. Workaround: start a transaction manually
in the consumer with the received `traceparent` and inject headers manually
on produce/publish.

annotations.title: Elastic .NET: Kafka instrumentation exists only in the CLR-profiler deployment, not the startup hook
annotations.cause: The startup-hook zero-code deployment covers neither Kafka nor RabbitMQ; the profiler that does is x64-only and caps at Confluent.Kafka <3.0.0.
annotations.explanation:
elastic-apm-dotnet 1.34.7 with the startup-hook zero-code deployment passes
HTTP and gRPC including baggage. Kafka and RabbitMQ are the only rows in the
profiler docs' technology table without the startup-hook marker: the agent's
own messaging instrumentation exists only in the CLR-profiler deployment,
which is x64-only on Windows and Linux ("ARM and 32-bit processes are not
supported") and even then caps at `Confluent.Kafka >=1.4.0 <3.0.0` and
`RabbitMQ.Client >=3.6.9 <7.0.0`.

Confluent.Kafka has no native `ActivitySource` for the agent's OpenTelemetry
bridge to pick up, so Kafka measures fully absent: `*->kafka` injects
nothing and `kafka->*` starts a new trace. (RabbitMQ trace context still
flows via RabbitMQ.Client 7.x's native ActivitySource — see
`elastic-dotnet-rabbitmq-native-no-baggage` for the baggage half.)

Workaround: inject/extract `traceparent`/`tracestate` manually around
Confluent.Kafka produce and consume using the agent's public API.

annotations.title: Elastic .NET: RabbitMQ trace context flows via the client's native ActivitySource, but baggage does not
annotations.cause: The Elastic agent has no RabbitMQ.Client 7 instrumentation; the client's own default propagation carries trace id and tracestate only, never baggage.
annotations.explanation:
`*->rabbitmq` injection and `rabbitmq->*` continuation both pass for
`traceparent`/`tracestate` on elastic-apm-dotnet 1.34.7 — not because the
agent instruments RabbitMQ (its own instrumentation is profiler-only and
caps at `RabbitMQ.Client <7.0.0`), but because RabbitMQ.Client 7.x ships
native `ActivitySource` instrumentation (PR #1261) that the agent's
OpenTelemetry bridge picks up.

That native path cannot carry baggage: its `DefaultContextExtractor` calls
`ExtractTraceIdAndState(...)` only. Baggage was addressed via an opt-in
package (PR #1528) that has never shipped stable (#1728, open since Nov
2024). Workaround: forward `baggage` as an application header in the AMQP
message properties yourself.

annotations.title: Elastic Ruby: gRPC support is experimental and manual, with no zero-code client or server path
annotations.cause: The Ruby agent instruments gRPC only via a hand-added ClientInterceptor at stub creation; the init-only setup adds none, and there is no server-side path.
annotations.explanation:
elastic-apm (Ruby) 4.9.0 passes `http->http` only. gRPC support exists but
is experimental and manual: "To instrument a client, add the
`ElasticAPM::GRPC::ClientInterceptor` as an `interceptor` at Stub creation".
The harness's init-only setup (`require 'elastic_apm'; ElasticAPM.start`)
adds no interceptor, so `*->grpc` carries nothing, and with no server-side
instrumentation `grpc->*` runs with no transaction and injects nothing on
the outbound leg.

What a user can do: wire the client interceptor into every stub. Nothing
documented covers the server side. The accurate claim is "no zero-code
gRPC", not "no gRPC at all".

annotations.title: Elastic Ruby: no bunny or client-level Kafka instrumentation, and the Racecar spy never reads headers
annotations.cause: The Ruby agent covers Kafka only via Racecar (whose spy never reads a trace_parent) and RabbitMQ only via Sneakers; rdkafka and bunny are uninstrumented.
annotations.explanation:
Nothing is injected on `*->kafka` or `*->rabbitmq` and nothing is extracted
on `kafka->*` or `rabbitmq->*` on elastic-apm (Ruby) 4.9.0. The supported
technologies page lists RabbitMQ only as "Sneakers (Experimental)" and no
Kafka client library at all; Kafka is covered only via the Racecar
framework.

Even under Racecar, consume-side continuation is impossible: the racecar spy
(`lib/elastic_apm/spies/racecar.rb`, added by PR #1284) calls
`ElasticAPM.start_transaction(kind, TYPE)` with no `trace_parent`, so it
never reads message headers.

No upstream issues request bunny or client-level Kafka (rdkafka/ruby-kafka)
instrumentation. Workaround: inject `traceparent`/`tracestate` into message
headers manually and start the consumer transaction with the received
`trace_parent`.

annotations.title: Elastic PHP: Kafka and RabbitMQ are not supported technologies; only http->http propagates
annotations.cause: elastic_apm instruments neither rdkafka nor php-amqplib: nothing is injected on produce/publish and consumed messages start a fresh trace on the outbound leg.
annotations.explanation:
On elastic_apm 1.17.0 (PHP 8.3, Apache mod_php + CLI workers) only
`http->http` propagates `traceparent`/`tracestate`. Kafka and RabbitMQ are
not in the agent's supported-technologies list: `http->kafka` and
`http->rabbitmq` inject nothing, and the CLI consumers do not extract, so
`kafka->http` and `rabbitmq->http` start a fresh trace (new trace-id, the
foreign tracestate entry lost) while `kafka->kafka`, `kafka->rabbitmq`,
`rabbitmq->kafka` and `rabbitmq->rabbitmq` carry nothing.

gRPC-outbound legs are covered separately (`php-grpc-client-not-instrumented`)
and gRPC-inbound is undeliverable in this topology (`php-no-grpc-server`).
Our references cite no upstream issue for PHP messaging support in this
agent.

annotations.title: New Relic agents carry no W3C baggage on any boundary
annotations.cause: Baggage is not part of New Relic's distributed-tracing model (traceparent, tracestate, newrelic); no agent forwards the header and no feature request exists.
annotations.explanation:
New Relic's "How distributed tracing works" defines the complete header
model as exactly three headers — `traceparent`, `tracestate` and the vendor
`newrelic` header. The seeded W3C `baggage` member is neither extracted nor
re-emitted by any of the seven agents on any of the 16 boundaries, even
where trace context continues perfectly (Python is 16/16 for trace
context).

An org-wide search for "baggage" across all New Relic agent repositories
returns three unrelated hits; no feature request for W3C baggage exists in
any of the seven agent repos. If you route on baggage, New Relic contributes
nothing on any protocol — carry it as an application header yourself.

links.title: How New Relic distributed tracing works

annotations.title: New Relic Java: Kafka DT header injection is opt-in via a class_transformer setting
annotations.cause: kafka-clients instrumentation is telemetry-only by default; header injection requires enabling the kafka-clients-spans-0.11.0.0 module in newrelic.yml.
annotations.explanation:
On newrelic-agent 9.4.0 with default configuration, every `*->kafka` leg
injects nothing. New Relic's Kafka docs make DT header injection opt-in:
`class_transformer: com.newrelic.instrumentation.kafka-clients-spans-0.11.0.0: enabled: true`,
warning that "the instrumentation adds a 150 to 200 byte payload to message
headers… we recommend testing… before enabling them in production". The
module exists in the agent repository.

The harness has not measured the opt-in (backlog: a
`newrelic-java-kafkaspans` variant), so whether it makes these cells pass is
documented, not verified. `kafka->kafka` and `rabbitmq->kafka` also fail on
the consume side (see `newrelic-java-messaging-inbound-never-accepted`).

links.title: New Relic Java agent — instrument Kafka message queues

annotations.title: New Relic Java: Kafka consumers and spring-rabbit listeners never accept inbound DT headers
annotations.cause: No spring-rabbit module: DT accept runs on the AMQP connection thread, not the listener's thread; the Kafka consumer instrumentation never accepts DT headers.
annotations.explanation:
Every messaging-inbound row is dead on newrelic-agent 9.4.0: `kafka->*` and
`rabbitmq->*` outbound calls carry no headers at all (no transaction is
active, so nothing is injected). spring-rabbit *publish* injects fine
(`http->rabbitmq`, `grpc->rabbitmq` pass).

Mechanism found in source: the agent has only `rabbit-amqp-2.7.0/5.0.0` and
`spring-kafka` modules — no spring-rabbit module at all. DT accept is woven
around `Consumer.handleDelivery` inside a transaction on the AMQP connection
thread, while spring-rabbit's listener container processes the message on a
different thread, outside that transaction. The Kafka consumer never
accepts either.

Workaround: in the listener, start a transaction with the New Relic agent
API and accept the message headers into it manually. No upstream issue
covers either gap — filing candidate.

annotations.title: New Relic Node: kafkajs instrumentation is behind a default-off feature flag
annotations.cause: feature_flags.js ships kafkajs_instrumentation: false; with it off the agent skips kafkajs entirely, so no headers are injected or accepted on Kafka.
annotations.explanation:
newrelic 14.3.10 is 9/16: HTTP, gRPC and RabbitMQ pass in both directions,
Kafka is dead in both directions. `lib/feature_flags.js` has
`kafkajs_instrumentation: false` (still false on main); with the flag off
the agent logs "skipping instrumentation of kafkajs" and does nothing. The
instrumentation shipped behind the flag in v11.19.0 (Jun 2024) and was never
promoted to default; the compatibility list also caps kafkajs at 2.2.4.

Empirically confirmed: rerunning with
`NEW_RELIC_FEATURE_FLAG_KAFKAJS_INSTRUMENTATION=true` flips all seven Kafka
boundaries to pass (W3C headers both directions) — 16/16, one environment
variable apart. Run archived at
`results/experiments/newrelic-node-kafkajs-flag.json`.

annotations.title: New Relic Go: nrsarama's producer injects DT headers into a throwaway map
annotations.cause: nrsarama calls InsertDistributedTraceHeaders on the carrier's embedded http.Header, bypassing the Set method that would copy headers into msg.Headers.
annotations.explanation:
go-agent v3.44.2 is 12/16 with manual wiring per vendor docs (nrgrpc,
nrsarama, nramqp). All Kafka-outbound legs are dead, and the root cause is a
visible bug in `nrsarama/producer.go`: it builds a carrier whose `Set` would
copy headers into `msg.Headers`, but then calls
`txn.InsertDistributedTraceHeaders(carrier.Header)` on the plain embedded
`http.Header` — bypassing `Set`, so the DT headers land in a discarded map
and never reach the Kafka message.

The consumer side (`nrsarama/consumer.go`) never calls
`AcceptDistributedTraceHeaders` either (it even calls *Insert* on the
consumed headers), and neither does the official example; the relay's manual
accept on consume is why `kafka->http/grpc/rabbitmq` pass here — that went
beyond the documented flow.

Workaround: call `txn.InsertDistributedTraceHeaders` yourself into a carrier
that writes `msg.Headers`, and accept manually on consume. Neither bug is
reported upstream (only the original 2019/2020 feature requests #98/#160) —
strong filing candidates.

links.title: go-agent nrsarama consumer example (no accept call)

annotations.title: New Relic .NET: RabbitMQ.Client 7's async IChannel API is not instrumented by the classic agent
annotations.cause: The agent instruments the classic IModel API that RabbitMQ.Client 7 removed; v7 support exists only via the default-off hybrid agent, which emits span links.
annotations.explanation:
newrelic-dotnet-agent 10.54.0 injects on all `*->kafka` legs but every
`*->rabbitmq` leg is dead, and `rabbitmq->*` never accepts. The agent's
instrumented-methods list is exclusively the classic `IModel.*` surface,
which RabbitMQ.Client 7 removed entirely; this relay uses 7.2.2's async-only
`IChannel.BasicPublishAsync`. The v7 async instrumentation PR #2890 was
closed unmerged on a `ValueTask<T>` blocker.

The compatibility docs' "7.1.2 verified" claim refers to the hybrid-agent
path (#2885: "RabbitMQ 7+ versions are supported with the new hybrid agent
feature in agent versions 10.49.0+"), which picks up the client's native
`ActivitySource` — but it is disabled by default and, per New Relic's docs,
"Distributed tracing works differently (span links vs. parent/child
relationships)". Default config: dead, exactly as measured.

What a user can do: enable the hybrid agent (accepting links rather than
continuity), pin RabbitMQ.Client <7, or insert/accept DT headers manually
with the agent API.

annotations.title: New Relic .NET: Confluent.Kafka produce injects, but consumed records are never accepted
annotations.cause: Confluent.Kafka instrumentation injects on produce but never accepts record headers into a transaction on consume, so outbound calls carry no headers.
annotations.explanation:
All `*->kafka` legs inject on newrelic-dotnet-agent 10.54.0, but every
`kafka->*` leg is dead: after a consume, outbound HTTP/gRPC/Kafka calls
carry no DT headers at all (no active transaction). FINDINGS records this as
"messaging-inbound all dead" and classes it with the consume-side
context-activation failures seen across vendors.

Our references do not include a source-level citation for the .NET Kafka
consume path; confirming the mechanism (whether the consume wrapper starts
a transaction and whether it calls accept on the record headers) in the
agent's Confluent.Kafka wrapper is the remaining investigation. No upstream
issue is cited. Workaround: start a transaction in the consume loop and
accept the record headers into it with the agent API.

annotations.title: New Relic Ruby: bunny publish injects only the legacy newrelic header, not W3C headers
annotations.cause: newrelic_rpm's bunny publish instrumentation emits the vendor newrelic header only; traceparent and tracestate are absent on every *->rabbitmq leg.
annotations.explanation:
newrelic_rpm 10.7.1 is 12/16 on W3C headers but 16/16 on the vendor header:
everything works, but bunny *publish* injects only the legacy `newrelic`
header. On all four `*->rabbitmq` boundaries `traceparent`/`tracestate` are
absent, so a W3C-only consumer downstream (or another vendor's agent) sees
nothing. Consume (`rabbitmq->*`) accepts and continues correctly.

Our references cite no upstream issue for this asymmetry. Workaround: insert
the W3C headers into the message headers yourself with the agent's
distributed-tracing API before publishing.

annotations.title: New Relic PHP does not instrument rdkafka; Kafka produce injects nothing
annotations.cause: The PHP agent's messaging support is php-amqplib publish only; rdkafka is unsupported, so no headers are injected into produced records.
annotations.explanation:
newrelic-php-agent 12.10.0.39 is 2/16: `http->http` (curl) and
`http->rabbitmq` (php-amqplib >= 3.7 publish instrumentation, agent >= 11.6)
carry all three trace headers. rdkafka is unsupported, so `http->kafka`
injects nothing; `kafka->kafka` and `rabbitmq->kafka` additionally fail on
the consume side (see `newrelic-php-cli-consumers-never-accept`).

Docker footgun worth knowing: `newrelic-install` symlinks the extension into
the extracted tarball directory by default — deleting the tarball leaves a
dangling symlink and a silently uninstrumented app; build with
`NR_INSTALL_USE_CP_NOT_LN=1`.

annotations.title: New Relic PHP: long-running CLI consumers never accept inbound context
annotations.cause: The PHP agent has no rdkafka consume or php-amqplib consume instrumentation, so the CLI worker processes never start a transaction from message headers.
annotations.explanation:
On newrelic-php-agent 12.10.0.39 every `kafka->*` and `rabbitmq->*` leg is
dead: the long-running CLI consumer workers never accept inbound context, so
outbound calls after a consume carry no headers (no transaction is active).
php-amqplib coverage is publish-side only, and rdkafka is unsupported
entirely.

Workaround: in the consumer loop, start a background transaction with the
agent API and accept the message headers manually. Our references cite no
upstream issue for consume-side support in the PHP agent.

annotations.title: OTel Python: confluent-kafka consumer links the producer context but never attaches it
annotations.cause: opentelemetry-instrumentation-confluent-kafka starts the consume span with the producer context as a link and never calls context.attach().
annotations.explanation:
The `poll()` wrapper in `opentelemetry-instrumentation-confluent-kafka` (0.65b0)
calls `_create_new_consume_span`, which does `start_span(..., links=links)`
with the extracted producer context as a *link*. The package never calls
`opentelemetry.context.attach()`, so the extracted context — and the baggage
riding on it — is never made current for the code that processes the message.
Every `kafka->*` leg therefore starts a new trace, and `baggage` and the
foreign `tracestate` entry are gone. All eight RabbitMQ boundaries pass via
`opentelemetry-instrumentation-pika`, whose per-message callback wrapper
extracts *and attaches* before invoking the handler — the failure is a
per-instrumentation design choice, not a language limitation.

Reported at least four times since 2023 across confluent-kafka, kafka-python
and aiokafka. The only fix attempt (PR #1678) was closed unmerged by the stale
bot; the maintainers' position (#3465) is that manually attaching the context
is the intended usage.

Workaround: after `poll()`, run `context.attach(propagate.extract(headers))`
yourself before making outbound calls. Upstream fix: attach the extracted
context (or make the consume span current) in the instrumentation, as the
pika instrumentation already does. No upstream issue names the *baggage*
loss specifically — filing candidate.

annotations.title: OTel .NET: Confluent.Kafka consumer spans link to the producer instead of continuing it
annotations.cause: Since 1.7.0 the .NET auto-instrumentation deliberately stops using the message-creation context as the consumer span's parent, per OTel messaging semconv.
annotations.explanation:
`opentelemetry-dotnet-instrumentation` 1.7.0 shipped #3434 / PR #3438 ("Do not
use message creation context as a parent for consumer spans for
`Confluent.Kafka` client instrumentation"). This follows the OTel messaging
semantic conventions, which "use span links as the default mechanism to
correlate producers and consumer(s)" (rule traced to OTEP-0220; parent-child
was later re-allowed as an *option* by semantic-conventions PR #1414). The
consumer span is therefore a new root: `kafka->*` starts a new trace, and
`baggage` and the foreign `tracestate` entry are not carried forward.

Maintainers treat same-symptom reports as by design: contrib #3995 (open,
"no bug here… as long as we are not switching to the modern [semconv]
version there is nothing to change") and #2351 (closed by-design).

Applications that need continuity or baggage across a Kafka hop must extract
the record headers and set the context themselves before making outbound
calls. All `*->kafka` injection, baggage included, works. No upstream issue
names the Kafka *baggage* loss — filing candidate.

annotations.title: OTel .NET: RabbitMQ.Client's native propagation continues the trace but carries no baggage
annotations.cause: RabbitMQ.Client 7's native ActivitySource extractor reads trace id and tracestate only; baggage lives in an opt-in package that never shipped stable.
annotations.explanation:
On `rabbitmq->*` the trace continues (`traceparent` and `tracestate` pass) but
`baggage` is dropped. The propagation here is RabbitMQ.Client's own, not
OTel's: 7.x ships native `ActivitySource` instrumentation (PR #1261) whose
`DefaultContextExtractor` calls `ExtractTraceIdAndState(...)` only — the word
"baggage" does not appear in the propagation code.

Baggage was addressed only via an opt-in companion package (PR #1528: "Making
it possible to override the default context propagation … to have proper
OpenTelemetry Baggage propagation"). That package, `RabbitMQ.Client.OpenTelemetry`,
has only ever shipped as 1.0.0-rc.1/rc.2 (#1728, open since Nov 2024), and
zero-code deployments never wire it in. The OTel auto-instrumentation tracks
deliver-span baggage as an unbuilt feature (#3662, open).

Version caveat for the passing half: parent-child continuity on consume is
the default only since RabbitMQ.Client 7.2.0 (`UsePublisherAsParent`, PR
#1779); on 7.0–7.1 the deliver activity was link-only. The relay pins 7.2.2.

annotations.title: OTel Ruby: bunny consumer drops the producer context and starts a new trace
annotations.cause: opentelemetry-instrumentation-bunny parents the process span on its own re-injected local headers and demotes the producer context to a span link.
annotations.explanation:
Injection into RabbitMQ (`*->rabbitmq`) via `opentelemetry-instrumentation-bunny`
0.25.0 is correct, baggage included. On consume, `with_process_span` in
`patch_helpers.rb` parents the process span on the instrumentation's own
`:tracer_receive_headers` (a local receive span it injected itself) and adds
the producer's real context only as a `Link`. Every `rabbitmq->*` leg starts
a new trace and loses baggage and the foreign tracestate entry.

Exact-match issue #526 ("Instead of propagating any contexts (including
baggage), the bunny instrumentation drops all contexts in the consumer and
starts a new trace") has been open since June 2023 with no fix PR.
Maintainers describe the behaviour as links-by-design per the OTel messaging
spec (discussion #1098).

Workaround: extract from the delivery headers and attach the context in the
consumer block before outbound calls. This is the same consume-side
activation gap seen in OTel Python (confluent-kafka) and OTel .NET (Kafka).

annotations.title: OTel Ruby: the gRPC instrumentation is client-only, so gRPC-inbound requests start a new trace
annotations.cause: opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc only instruments outbound calls; there is no server-side instrumentation for the plain grpc gem.
annotations.explanation:
The contrib gRPC instrumentation (donated from
hibachrach/opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc via PR #1164, Sep 2024,
answering a request open since 2020) is explicitly client-only — its README
warns "Right now, the gem only instruments outbound requests to gRPC
services". It *is* bundled in `opentelemetry-instrumentation-all`, so the
accurate statement is "loaded but client-only", and even client injection
requires manually wiring the interceptor into stubs. Server spans exist only
for the Gruf framework.

With no server-side extraction, `grpc->*` legs run with no incoming context;
outbound calls start a fresh trace and baggage/tracestate are lost.

Workaround: add a server interceptor that extracts from the call metadata and
attaches the context. No upstream issue requests server-side `grpc` gem
support — filing candidate.

links.title: opentelemetry-ruby-contrib gruf README (server spans for Gruf only)

annotations.title: OTel PHP: rdkafka producev() injection silently no-ops unless the $headers argument is present
annotations.cause: ext-opentelemetry drops arguments a pre-hook adds to a native function call, so the rdkafka instrumentation's injected $headers never reach producev().
annotations.explanation:
The ExtRdKafka instrumentation *does* set `$params[4]` (the `$headers` slot)
from its pre-hook unconditionally. But the `ext-opentelemetry` extension
silently drops arguments *added* to internal functions ever since argument
expansion was disabled to prevent a segfault (PR #84, formalised in PR #120;
original crash opentelemetry-php #1155). A naive
`producev($partition, 0, $payload)` therefore gets no headers at all, while
`producev($partition, 0, $payload, null, [])` — an explicit empty array —
makes injection (baggage included) work. Verified empirically both ways; the
drop produced no error_log line in our runs.

Escape hatch, documented only in the extension repo's README:
`opentelemetry.allow_stack_extension=On`. With that ini set, the naive call
injects traceparent, tracestate and baggage and `http->kafka` /
`kafka->kafka` flip to pass (run archived at
`results/experiments/otel-php-allow-stack-extension.json`). Neither the
argument requirement nor the ini setting is mentioned in the ExtRdKafka README.

Consume-side rdkafka extraction is correct (`kafka->http` passes) — this
asymmetry is outbound-only. No upstream issue exists — filing candidate
against open-telemetry/opentelemetry-php.

annotations.title: OTel PHP: no php-amqplib instrumentation exists, so every RabbitMQ leg loses context
annotations.cause: opentelemetry-php-contrib has no instrumentation for php-amqplib; its only AMQP coverage is the PECL ext-amqp client, a different library.
annotations.explanation:
The opentelemetry-php-contrib instrumentation tree has no `PhpAmqpLib`
entry. Its only AMQP coverage is `ExtAmqp` (the PECL `ext-amqp` client), and
even there consumers are manual by design. Nothing is injected on
`*->rabbitmq`, and nothing is extracted on `rabbitmq->*`; where the outbound
HTTP client is instrumented (`rabbitmq->http`) it injects a fresh trace.

Consumer hooks are structurally hard in PHP (opentelemetry-php #937: "You
cannot hook an anonymous function, only methods" — consume callbacks are
closures).

Workaround: use the OTel PHP propagator API to inject into the message's
application headers on publish and extract/attach in the consume callback.
No upstream feature request for php-amqplib exists — filing candidate
(php-amqplib is the dominant PHP AMQP client).
